details:
I have NAT64 and DNS64 configured on my network, to enable some devices to drop their IPv4 address, but still maintain connectivity to IPv4-only servers via a NAT64 gateway.

This also sometimes causes devices that still are running Dual Stack (like Windows) to connect to an IPv4 target via the IPv4-mapped IPv6 address, which so far has never been a problem for any other application.

VRChat seems to be a case where it is and it seems to fail to connect.

When I disable DNS64, so no IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are returned anymore, I can login to VRChat without an issue. If I re-enable it, VRChat will try to connect to the world and time out consistently.

I don't know exactly which part of this makes it fail, but it would nice to see this fixed so VRChat doesn't fail in networks with modern networking technologies available.

EDIT: Note that DNS64 only generates IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses for domains that don't already have a AAAA DNS record. So it seems that VRChat expects a connection via IPv4 and doesn't handle it properly that the connection is established via an IPv6 socket.

(I have only verified this behavior on Windows, though it sounds likely that it would also affect other platforms)
title: VRChat connections time out if the network has NAT64 and DNS64
